title: Speaking Part 1 — react, answer, expand
note:
The ladder is the default's formula: react, answer, then expand with a reason, an example and a contrast. IT IS A MENU, NOT A TEMPLATE. A third of the answers in this file stop at two, three or four moves, because a real Part 1 turn does. Using all five on every question is what makes a candidate sound rehearsed, and that is marked down under Discourse Management — so the corpus has to vary, or a student learns the pattern instead of the phrases. It is not new to this repo — part1-structure.json's phraseBank already holds it as five steps, and this file is that bank turned into something a student does rather than reads.

THE REACTION IS PREPENDED. Level 1 is the bare answer a student gives unprompted; round 1 puts a reaction in FRONT of it. The screen performs the rule, which is the one thing a phrase list cannot do. Every other move is appended.

Every level is written in full by a person. The engine never composes an answer — it only chooses which level to show. Three voices run the same ladder at the same depth, so switching changes whose life it is, not how developed the answer is.

icon and color are deliberately absent. The old bank stored an emoji and a hex per step, and presentation inside a data file is how a page ends up carrying five saturated hues from no palette in this product.

THE LIVES ARE FUNCHAL TEENAGERS. All three voices are fifteen- to sixteen-year-olds living in or around Funchal, Madeira — not students-vs-graduates-vs-professionals. They differ in personality (outgoing, quieter, more into nature and sport), not in life stage, and the places named are real Funchal geography: Zona Velha, Avenida do Mar, Praia Formosa, the Monte cable car, the levadas, Mercado dos Lavradores, Porto Santo as the island everyone escapes to by ferry.

x.name: React
x.hint: how you feel about the question, before you answer it

e.name: Example
e.hint: one specific thing from your own life

c.name: Contrast
c.hint: the other side, so the answer sounds balanced

phraseBank.heading: Reacting — not keen
phrases: I can't say I'm keen on…
I've never been that bothered about…

phraseBank.heading: Reacting — fronted, and worth two criteria
phraseBank.note: These are clefts. They mark the discourse and count as complex structures at the same time.
phrases: The thing I love about… is…
If there's one thing I…, it's…

tip: Don't memorise answers. Most good answers use two or three of these moves, not all five — match the shape to the question, and give a small question a short answer. An answer that follows the shape sounds natural; an answer that recites it does not.
